subject: Human Body
title: Fingerprints
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fingerprints.

hook.text: Your fingerprints formed before birth and will stay unchanged for life. Even identical twins have different patterns.

buildup.text: Fingerprint ridges form at 10 weeks of fetal development. Random pressures in the womb create unique ridge patterns.

discovery.text: Ridges improve grip by increasing friction.

twist.text: Koalas have fingerprints nearly identical to humans.

climax.text: Fingerprints are unique, permanent, and functional.

punchline.text: No one shares your fingerprints. Not even your twin.

quiz.question: Why are identical twins' fingerprints different?
options: DNA determines fingerprint patterns and twins have different DNA
Random pressures during fetal development create unique patterns
Fingerprints change after birth based on hand usage
